analysis.title: European Retailing: Key trends in apparel retailing: +ve NXT; ITX 9M preview
key_insights: Channel shift online has accelerated in mainland Europe, and RBC expects stronger online and omnichannel chains such as NEXT, Zalando and Inditex to outperform. Consumers remain highly value and promo focused.
Top picks are NEXT and Zalando. H&M and ABF valuations look fuller. RBC sees potential for sector margin pressure from higher costs and promo activity.
Inditex 9M results are due December 2. RBC forecasts Q3 sales of EUR10.6bn (+8% cc), PBT EUR2.54bn and EPS EUR0.63 (+8% yoy), slightly below consensus EUR0.64.
RBC models Q3 gross margin down 15bps yoy and EBIT margin down 30bps yoy on elevated air freight and online delivery costs, partly offset by slower D&A growth.

Inditex is expanding non-Zara concepts internationally. Massimo Dutti opened in SoHo New York, Bershka in Miami and Brazil, and Zara reopened its Fifth Avenue flagship with more than 20 US projects planned for 2027.
Inditex has c.2.5% of the global fashion market and only 0.5% in the US. RBC sees a better US outlook due to more cities, shorter lease terms and better store-opening data from online.
Gross margin correlates with EUR/USD on a 6-month lag. A weaker EUR helps sales next year but pressures gross margin, so RBC sees gross and operating margin slightly down in FY28, especially in H1.
RBC forecasts Inditex EPS growth of c.7.5% this year and 9% next year, with ROCE around 40%. Inditex rated Outperform, DCF PT EUR63 (WACC 6.8%, terminal growth 2.5%), upside EUR71, downside EUR46.

Second-hand apparel has doubled over 5 years to about 10% of apparel sales and RBC expects over 40% further growth to 12-13%. Resale cannibalisation is a sector risk, but Zara, H&M, Zalando and ASOS are responding well.

JD Sports PT raised from 90p to 100p, Sector Perform kept. FY27-28 PBT cut 1-2% on FX and space, EPS up 1-2% on buybacks. Expects PBT down at least 15% this year, trades c.8x CY27e P/E with 11% FCF yield.
JD Q3 online sales grew +0.8% yoy vs +5.2% in H1, APAC was weak on Australia, and underlying price investment continues at 50bps.
Large chains in Spain keep taking share from independents and department stores, supporting Inditex in its home market.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong omnichannel model, US expansion and ROCE around 40% support sales and EPS growth of 9% next year.
tension_points.bear_case: Freight costs and a weaker EUR pressure gross and EBIT margin, with EBIT margin down 30bps in Q3.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Higher-than-expected discounting or a slowdown in sales momentum, per the downside scenario.
